info.title: Ironfang Render API
info.summary: Screenshots, PDFs, dynamic images and video through one API.
info.description:
Ironfang Render renders web pages to images, PDFs and video. Give it a URL or a
block of HTML and get the finished asset without running a browser.

## No attribution on your output

Nothing you render through the API carries an Ironfang badge or watermark,
whatever your billing state. Only the anonymous free tools on
ironfang.com mark their output.

## Authentication

Every request carries an API key as a bearer token:

```
Authorization: Bearer rw_live_...
```

Keys are created in the portal at https://portal.ironfang.com. They are shown
once at creation and stored only as a hash, so a lost key is replaced rather
than recovered.

## Responses are bytes, not JSON

`/v1/screenshot`, `/v1/pdf`, `/v1/image/{id}` and `/v1/video` return the
rendered file directly. `/v1/site-preview` returns a multipart payload with
the poster and MP4. Only errors and the metadata endpoints return JSON.

## Billing

Ironfang Render has no plans or credits. Usage is billed to your
organisation's Ironfang billing account, which every product shares
(`/billing/v1`, managed in the portal). Each kind of work counts against a
meter, and each meter has a monthly free allowance (UTC calendar months);
beyond it, usage is pay-as-you-go at graduated rates once paid usage is
enabled on the billing account. The catalogue of meters, allowances and
rates is `GET /billing/v1/catalogue`.

| Work | Meter | Counts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Screenshot, signed screenshot | `render.screenshot` | 1 per screenshot |
| PDF | `render.pdf` | 1 per PDF of at most 100 pages |
| Template image, signed image | `render.image` | 1 per image |
| QR code | `render.qr` | 1 per code; a free utility, never charged |
| Clip, 1080p (`vertical`, `landscape`) | `render.video_second_fhd` | output seconds, rounded up per clip |
| Clip, `720p` or `square` | `render.video_second_hd` | output seconds, rounded up per clip |
| Site preview | `render.site_preview_second` | output seconds, rounded up per preview |

Every billable request is admitted before any work starts: the most it
can count is reserved, and a request that cannot be admitted is refused
with nothing done. What the work actually produced is committed when it
succeeds - never more than was reserved - and a failure, a refused input
or a cancellation commits nothing. A clip reserves its duration; a site
preview reserves the 60 second limit and commits its real length. Billable
responses say what they counted in `X-Ironfang-Meter` and
`X-Ironfang-Quantity`; `GET /v1/usage` reports the period.

A billing refusal answers with a stable code in the usual error body:
`free_allowance_exhausted`, `account_budget_exhausted` or
`product_budget_exhausted` (429); `paid_usage_paused`, `payment_required`,
`payment_action_required` or `account_restricted` (402);
`product_not_eligible` (403); `account_closed` (410);
`operation_too_large` (413); `billing_temporarily_unavailable` (503, with
`Retry-After`). An API key on an account that belongs to no Ironfang
organisation is `403 account_not_linked`.

A PDF may have at most 100 pages. A longer document is refused with
`422 pdf_too_long` and nothing is counted.

## Caching

An identical request made again within **ten minutes** of the render that
produced it may be served from cache: `X-Ironfang-Cache: hit`,
`X-Ironfang-Quantity: 0`, nothing reserved and nothing counted. The cache
is per instance and bounded in size, so an entry can be evicted sooner and
a hit is never guaranteed; after ten minutes the same request is a new,
billable render. PDFs are never cached. Set `no_cache: true` to force a
fresh render, which is billable; the flag is deliberately excluded from
the cache key, so two fresh requests do not hit each other's results.

## Rate limits

Two rate limits apply, both per minute:

- **120 renders per account**, and
- **60 renders per target host**, counted across all customers.

The second protects the sites being rendered: one API call is a full page
load, so a victim's exposure must not scale with our customer count. Both
are checked after the cache and before admission, so a blocked call
reserves and costs nothing.

## Capacity limits

Three more limits are the same for every account, and no billing setting
lifts them. They are refused with Ironfang Render's own codes, never a
billing code, and a refused call reserves and costs nothing.

- **2 browser operations in progress per account.** Screenshots, PDFs,
  template images and site previews count together, however they
  arrived: synchronous requests (signed URLs included) and durable jobs a
  worker is running, across the whole service. A synchronous request
  over the limit is `429 concurrency_limit` with `Retry-After`; a signed
  URL, whose caller is a browser or a link-preview crawler, first waits
  up to 10 seconds for one to finish. A durable job over it is not
  refused: it waits in the queue until one of the account's operations
  finishes. QR codes and clips use no browser and do
  not count. A cache hit uses no browser either.
- **1,000 unfinished jobs per account** (queued, running or being
  cancelled). A job or a batch that would take the account past it is
  `429 queue_full`, with `Retry-After`; a batch is refused whole, and no
  job of it is created.

## Bot protection

Ironfang Render does not attempt to circumvent bot protection, CAPTCHAs or
paywalls. A challenge page renders as the challenge page. This is a
deliberate limit, not a bug.

## For agents and tools

The canonical base URL is https://api.ironfang.com/render. Every operation
has a stable `operationId`. Every error an operation returns is JSON of the
shape `{"error": {"code", "message", "docs"}, "request_id"}`: branch on
`code` and the HTTP status, never on `message`. The machine-readable index
of the Ironfang APIs is https://ironfang.com/.well-known/api-catalog, and
https://ironfang.com/llms.txt is a plain-text map of them for a language
model. Ironfang Render is also available as MCP tools at
https://mcp.ironfang.com/mcp (see https://ironfang.com/docs/mcp). Renderwolf
is the name the product launched under, not a separate product; its
`/renderwolf` prefix and `X-Renderwolf-*` headers were retired on
28 September 2026, and the prefix now answers `410`.

servers.description: Production, unpartitioned - retained for existing clients

post.description:
Supply exactly one of `url` or `html`. Returns the image bytes.
Counts one `render.screenshot`.

element.summary: One element, on a dark-mode page

post.description:
Styled, optionally logo-bearing QR codes, drawn natively and
**verified before delivery**: every response is decoded and compared
to `data` on the way out. A code that would not scan is a
`422 unscannable` and nothing is counted - the guarantee is the
feature.

A logo forces the highest error-correction level and is composited
over the center on a knockout tile (`logo_pad`). Send it inline as a
`data:` URI (`logo`) or by URL (`logo_url`); remote logos face the
same target guard and rate caps as screenshot URLs.

QRs are deterministic, so identical requests hit the cache and cache
hits count nothing. Each code counts one `render.qr`, a free utility:
it shows in usage and is never charged. Output never carries a
badge - a mark inside a scannable symbol would corrupt it.

To place a QR inside a stored template render, use the `qr` object
on `POST /v1/image/{id}` instead - each entry becomes a
`{{qr.<name>}}` variable holding a data URI.

branded.summary: Rounded style with a centered logo

post.description:
Supply exactly one of `url` or `html`. Returns `application/pdf`.

`header_html` and `footer_html` are Chromium print templates: they
support the classes `date`, `title`, `url`, `pageNumber` and
`totalPages`, which Chromium substitutes at print time.

Counts one `render.pdf`. A PDF may have at most 100 pages; a document
that prints to more is refused with `422 pdf_too_long` and nothing is
counted. PDFs are never cached.

invoice.summary: An invoice with a page footer

post.description:
A background, captions that appear on a schedule, an optional
watermark and an optional audio bed, encoded to MP4.

Rendered inside the request, so clips are capped at 60 seconds. A
clip counts its output seconds, rounded up: `render.video_second_fhd`
for the 1080p sizes (`vertical`, `landscape`) and
`render.video_second_hd` for `720p` and `square`. Its duration is
reserved before the encode and committed when the clip is delivered;
a clip that fails to render counts nothing.

Every asset URL is fetched by us through the same guard a screenshot
target faces, and each is capped at 64 MB.

captioned.summary: A captioned vertical clip on a solid colour

overBackground.summary: Over an image, with a logo and music

501.description: This deployment has no encoder configured.

post.description:
Loads and settles a website, preloads lazy content, then records a
top-to-bottom browser motion at 30 frames per second. `per_page` moves
one viewport at a time and pauses for 750ms between steps.
`single_sweep` makes one continuous eased pass. Sticky and fixed
elements behave as they do in the browser.

The response is one `multipart/form-data` payload containing the first
video frame as `poster.jpg` and the H.264 video as `preview.mp4`.
Ironfang Render calculates the duration from the page height and selected
motion, up to a 60 second hard limit. A preview counts its output
seconds, rounded up, against `render.site_preview_second`: the 60
second limit is reserved before the recording starts and the real
length is committed when the preview is delivered. Failed work counts
nothing and cached repeats are free.

This endpoint is available on the product-partitioned Ironfang Render URL
only. It has no unprefixed `/v1/site-preview` compatibility route.

501.description: This deployment does not have browser video capture configured.

get.description: Paged newest first. Follow next_cursor until empty; `total` is the whole count and does not change between pages. summary=true returns an empty html field; fetch a template by ID to edit or render it.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque next_cursor from the previous page; empty means the first page.

parameters.name: summary
parameters.description: Omit HTML bodies from the database read.

200.description:
Your templates, wrapped in a `templates` property - not a bare
array. Clients that iterate must read `templates`.

400.description: Malformed cursor, repeated or unknown parameter, or limit outside 1-100.

post.description:
Store HTML containing `{{placeholders}}`. Render it with
`POST /v1/image/{id}`, supplying values for the placeholders.

get.description: Returns a stored rendering template belonging to the authenticated account, including its HTML and output dimensions.

put.description: Replaces the authenticated account's stored template with the supplied name, HTML and dimensions. Subsequent renders use the updated template.

delete.description: Removes a stored template from the authenticated account so it can no longer be used for new template renders.

post.description:
Substitutes `vars` into the template's `{{placeholders}}` and renders it
at the template's own width and height. Returns the image bytes.

Returns a URL that renders on GET without an API key - safe to put in an `` tag or an email. The URL is bound to your account, so renders through it are admitted and counted against your organisation's billing account like any other. A signed URL expires after 30 days unless `ttl_hours` says otherwise: any number of hours, or `0` for a URL that never expires, which is what an `og:image` tag needs. The response says when the URL expires. Requires signing to be configured on the deployment; returns `501` otherwise.

501.description: Signing is not configured on this deployment.

get.description:
The endpoint a signed URL points at. Takes no API key - the signature is
the credential - so it can be embedded directly in HTML or email. Call
`POST /v1/sign` to mint one rather than constructing it by hand.

parameters.name: exp
parameters.description:
Expiry, in unix seconds, part of the signed payload. `0` never
expires.

404.description: Signing is not configured on this deployment.

get.summary: What Ironfang Render does, is building and does not offer
get.description:
A dated statement of capabilities with a status of `live`, `planned`
or `not_offered`. Public and cacheable; the comparison pages are
checked against the same file, so nothing is advertised before it is
live.

post.description:
The same renders as the synchronous endpoints - `kind` is one of
`screenshot`, `pdf`, `qr`, `image`, `clip` or `site_preview` and
`request` is that endpoint's body (an `image` job names its
`template` inside `request`) - accepted with `202` and run by a
worker. Poll the job, or cancel it, then collect the result while it
is hosted: 24 hours, private, through a signed link valid for 15
minutes. A process restart after the `202` never loses the job.

Send `Idempotency-Key` on every submission. The same key with the same
request returns the existing job with `200`; the same key with a
different request is a `409 idempotency_conflict`. `external_id` is
your own reference, up to 120 characters.

Billing: the most the job can count is reserved on your billing
account when it is accepted - in the same step, so a job you were told
about always holds its reservation, and a refusal leaves no job. The
one reservation is kept across retries of the job and committed, with
what the job produced, when it succeeds; a site preview reserves the
60 second limit and commits its real length. A job that fails,
is cancelled while queued, or is cancelled while running without a
usable output, counts nothing. The job's `usage` says what it holds:
`{"meter", "reserved", "committed"}`.

Capacity: an account may have 1,000 unfinished jobs (queued, running
or being cancelled); a job past that is `429 queue_full` and is not
created. A job that uses the browser runs in one of the account's 2
browser slots, shared with its synchronous renders; while both are
busy it waits in the queue rather than being refused.

request.description: The synchronous endpoint's request body for that kind.

202.description: The job was accepted; the body is the job resource.

200.description: The same Idempotency-Key and request were seen before; this is that job.

403.description: The key carries no `render:render` scope, or is not account-backed.

404.description: The template named by an image job does not exist.

409.description: `idempotency_conflict`: the key was used with a different request.

501.description: This deployment cannot render clips or site previews.

get.description: Newest first. `status` filters; `active` includes queued, running and cancellation_requested. `limit` up to 100; pass `next_cursor` back to continue.

400.description: `bad_request`: `cursor` is not one this endpoint issued.

403.description: The key carries no `render:render` scope, or is not account-backed.

get.description:
`status` is `queued`, `running`, `cancellation_requested`,
`succeeded`, `failed` or `cancelled`. A succeeded job carries
`result` with `content_type`, `bytes`, `sha256`, `expires_at` and,
while hosted, a signed `url` valid for 15 minutes. A failed job
carries `error.code` and `error.message`. `usage` names the meter
and the quantity reserved and committed. The submitted request is
never returned; `request_summary` is the redacted shape.

404.description: No such job on this account.

delete.description: A queued job is cancelled and its reservation released at once; a running one stops at its next safe point, and counts only if it had already produced a usable output.

200.description: The job, cancelled or with cancellation requested.

404.description: No such job on this account.

get.description:
Redirects (`302`) to a signed download link valid for 15 minutes; the
link needs no API key. The hosted result is kept for 24 hours after
success, privately, on Ironfang's side - not permanent hosting.

302.description: Redirect to the signed download link.

404.description: No such job on this account.

410.description: `result_expired`: the hosted result is gone; run the job again.

get.description: The link a job's `result.url` points at. The signature is the authorisation; it expires after 15 minutes.

200.description: The result bytes with their recorded content type.

get.description: Tenant-scoped metadata, newest first by creation time and ID. Equal timestamps retain stable pagination. Newer insertions do not appear on subsequent pages; refresh the first page to see them. No input payloads or child job bodies in batch summaries. A final page has an empty next_cursor. Responses are no-store. The JWT portal twin has the same response and pagination contract.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Pass next_cursor from the preceding page; empty means the first page.

400.description: Malformed cursor, repeated/unknown parameter or limit outside 1–100.

403.description: The caller cannot read this collection.

post.description:
One `default` request plus `items` that override parts of it, merged
one level deep: an item's field wins, everything else comes from the
default. The default is written for the batch's `kind`, so it applies
only to items of that kind; an item that names a different kind stands
on its own request, and any item may carry its own `delivery`. Every item is validated as a single job would be,
and an unknown field is refused rather than ignored, because a typo
that is silently dropped is a render spent on the wrong thing.

The batch is accepted or refused whole. Every item is validated before
any is stored, and every item is admitted on your billing account in
one step, so a batch any item of which cannot be admitted is refused
with the billing code, reserves nothing and leaves no jobs behind.
Each item then commits or releases on its own as its job finishes.
A validation error names the item that was wrong. A batch that would
take the account past 1,000 unfinished jobs is refused whole the
same way, with `429 queue_full`.

Items are ordinary jobs: poll them individually, or poll the batch for
the aggregate. There is no ZIP of results - configure a storage
destination if you want the output collected in one place.

Send `Idempotency-Key` to make the submission safe to retry: the same
key returns the batch it first created, with its jobs and another
`202`, instead of a second set of jobs and a second reservation. The
request is not compared with the first. Poll the batch for its
current counts.

default.description: The request every item starts from.

202.description: The batch was accepted; the body carries the batch and one job per item.

400.description: Invalid submission, or `batch_too_large`. The message names the item.

403.description: The key carries no `render:render` scope, or is not account-backed.

get.description:
`counts` totals the items by state and `done` is true once none of
them can change. `jobs` is the full job resource for every item.

200.description: The batch, its counts and its jobs.

404.description: No such batch on this account.

post.description:
A destination is created once and named by id from every job, so a
signing secret or a set of S3 keys is sent to us on one request and
never appears in a job body again.

A `webhook` destination needs a public `https` URL. The response
carries `signing_secret` **once**: we keep only an encrypted copy,
so there is no endpoint that can show it to you again.

`signing_secret` is 64 hex characters: the hex encoding of a 32-byte
key. Each delivery carries `Ironfang-Signature: v1=<hex>`, the
HMAC-SHA256 of `<Ironfang-Timestamp>.<raw body>` keyed with those 32
bytes - decode the secret from hex before verifying, rather than
using its text. The SDKs' `verifyWebhook` / `verify_webhook` take
the secret as shown and decode it (from 3.0.1).

An `s3` destination needs `bucket`, `region`, `access_key` and
`secret_key`; `endpoint` (for a non-AWS provider), `path_style` and
`prefix` are optional. Scope the credentials to the prefix you give
us. They are never returned after creation.

Needs the `render:destinations` scope, which maps to the
`destinations.manage` permission.

201.description: The destination. A webhook also carries `signing_secret`, shown once: 64 hex characters encoding the 32-byte HMAC key. Decode hex before verifying signatures.

400.description: `bad_destination`: not a public https URL, or missing bucket credentials.

501.description: This deployment has no credential vault configured.

get.description: Live destinations, newest first. Secrets and credentials are never included.

403.description: The key carries no `render:destinations` scope, or is not account-backed.

get.description: Returns a delivery destination belonging to the authenticated account. Stored delivery credentials are not included in the response.

404.description: No such destination on this account.

patch.description:
`name` and `enabled` only. An address or a credential is not edited in
place - create a new destination and point your jobs at it, so a
delivery's history always says where it actually went. Re-enabling
clears the failure count.

404.description: No such destination on this account.

delete.description:
It stops receiving anything and leaves the list. Its past deliveries
stay, so history still reads true.

404.description: No such destination on this account.

post.description:
A webhook receives a signed `render.destination.test` event; a
bucket has a uniquely named object written to it. Always `200`: the
body's `ok` says whether the destination answered, and `error` says
what went wrong if it did not.

404.description: No such destination on this account.

get.description:
One row per authenticated render in the last seven days, newest
first, synchronous calls and jobs alike: kind, outcome, safe error
code, cache hit or miss, the `meter` it counted against and the
`quantity` it committed (0 for a cache hit or a failure), response
size and type, duration, the target's origin and path, the names of
the option fields supplied, and the request id you can quote to
support.

It is diagnostic, not replay. Nothing here can rebuild the request:
header and cookie values, HTML, template variables, URL query strings
and signatures are never recorded. Retention is seven days for every
account.

`id` matches the request id, a job id or your own `X-Request-ID`,
which is how you arrive here from an error message.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Request id, job id or your X-Request-ID

get.description:
Newest first, optionally for one `destination`. A delivery is
`pending`, `delivering`, `delivered` or `failed`; `failed` means it
used up its attempts. Delivery state never affects the job's own
outcome. Filters apply before the cursor boundary. `pending` selects
pending deliveries with no attempts; `retrying` selects pending deliveries
with at least one attempt. `job_id` selects one owned job.

200.description: Deliveries and next_cursor, with no-store caching.

400.description: Invalid, repeated or unknown query parameter.

get.summary: One delivery, with the body it posted
get.description:
The list omits payloads because they are the largest part of a
delivery and are wanted one at a time, when something has gone wrong.
This returns the body exactly as it went on the wire, plus
`payload_timestamp` and `payload_signature` - the two values the
signature is computed over - so you can reproduce the HMAC check
against your own secret and see where it diverges.

`response_body` is what your endpoint sent back, bounded to 4 KB.

Bodies are kept for `payload_retention_days` (7) after the attempt
and then blanked; the delivery row itself stays, so the history of
what was sent and how it went is not lost with it.

200.description: The delivery. Payload is absent once purged.

404.description: No such delivery on this account.

post.description:
Puts a delivery back on the queue with a fresh attempt ladder, for
after you have fixed whatever was wrong. The webhook body is rebuilt
at send time, so the result link in it is good for 15 minutes from
then rather than from the original attempt.

404.description: No such delivery on this account.

get.description:
This UTC calendar month's Ironfang Render usage from your
organisation's billing account: for every Render meter, what was used,
how much of it the free allowance covered, what is held by work in
flight, and what the settled usage costs before tax. The whole
account - every product, budgets, statements - is `/billing/v1`.

An env bootstrap key, or a deployment with billing off, is unmetered
and answers `{"unmetered": true}`.

apiKey.description: An API key from the portal, sent as `Authorization: Bearer rw_live_...`.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description:
Makes a submission safe to retry. Any string up to 255 characters;
surrounding whitespace is ignored and a longer key is a `400
bad_request`. A key is remembered per account for as long as the job
it created exists, and has no expiry of its own. Jobs and batches
keep separate key spaces.

A job submitted again under its key returns the existing job with
`200` when the request is the same, and is a `409
idempotency_conflict` when it differs. A batch submitted again under
its key returns the batch the key first created, with its jobs and
`202`; the request is not compared, so a batch has no conflict
response.

SyncIdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
SyncIdempotencyKey.description:
Makes a synchronous render happen, and count, at most once. Any string
up to 255 characters, remembered per account. The first request under
a key is admitted and rendered as usual; a synchronous result is not
kept, so the same request again under the key is a `409
idempotency_key_used` and reserves nothing - send a new key to render
again. A different request under a used key is a `409
idempotency_conflict`. An identical request inside the cache window is
still served from cache.

Meter.description:
The billing meter this request counted against, e.g.
`render.screenshot`. Present on every billable response, cache hits
included.

Quantity.description:
The quantity this request committed to its meter: 1 for a unit
render, output seconds (rounded up) for video, `0` for a cache hit or
an unmetered key. Read it to log usage per request without polling
`/v1/usage`.

Image.description: The rendered image. `png` unless `format: jpeg` was requested.

X-Ironfang-Cache.description: `hit` when served from cache, in which case it counted nothing.

X-Ironfang-Render-Ms.description: Render time in milliseconds, excluding any requested delay.

X-Ironfang-Delay-Ms.description: The `delay_ms` actually waited, when one was requested.

X-Ironfang-Captured-At.description:
RFC 3339 timestamp of a fresh capture. Present only on
`no_cache` renders, where the response is also `no-store` - the
pairing is what makes a capture usable as evidence.

SitePreview.description: The poster image and scrolling MP4 returned as two file parts.

X-Ironfang-Quantity.description:
Output seconds committed, rounded up; the poster is included. `0`
on a cache hit.

X-Ironfang-Output-Seconds.description: Calculated video length in seconds. Present on fresh renders.

poster.description: JPEG first frame, suitable for a video poster.

BadRequest.description: Malformed body, or neither/both of `url` and `html`.

Unauthorized.description: Missing, malformed, revoked or unknown API key.

NotFound.description: No such template, or not yours.

RateLimited.description:
Rate limits and exhausted billing allowances share this status,
separated by `error.code`:

- `rate_limited` - your account exceeded 120 renders/minute
- `target_rate_limited` - the site being rendered is being hit too hard
  across all customers (60/minute per host)
- `clip_busy`, `preview_busy` - every encoder or preview slot on the
  worker is in use; `Retry-After` says when to come back
- `concurrency_limit` - your account already has 2 browser
  operations in progress, synchronous renders and running jobs
  together; retry after `Retry-After`, or submit a durable job,
  which waits for a free slot instead of being refused
- `queue_full` - your account already has 1,000 unfinished jobs, or
  the batch would take it past that; nothing was enqueued
- `free_allowance_exhausted` - this month's free allowance for the
  meter is used up and paid usage is not enabled
- `account_budget_exhausted`, `product_budget_exhausted` - the
  billing account's monthly limit, or Ironfang Render's, is reached
- `exemption_limit_reached` - an exempt account's agreed limit is reached

The rate and capacity limits clear by themselves, so retry with
backoff, after `Retry-After` where it is sent. The billing codes do
not: enable paid usage or raise the limit in Billing, or wait for the
month to roll over. Nothing was reserved or counted. Branch on the
code rather than the status.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying, on the refusals that clear by themselves.

Forbidden.description:
`insufficient_scope` - the key does not carry the scope;
`account_not_linked` - the key's account belongs to no Ironfang
organisation, so its usage cannot be billed; `product_not_eligible` -
paid use of Ironfang Render needs an eligible billing account.

IdempotencyConflict.description:
`idempotency_key_used` - this Idempotency-Key already made its render
(or is making it, or failed); nothing was reserved again.
`idempotency_conflict` - the key was used for a different request.

BillingRefused.description:
Paid usage cannot be billed: `paid_usage_paused`, `payment_required`,
`payment_action_required` or `account_restricted`. Resolve it in
Billing; nothing was reserved or counted. The same body can also
carry `account_closed` (410) and `operation_too_large` (413).

BillingUnavailable.description:
`billing_temporarily_unavailable` - the billing ledger could not admit
the request just now. Retry after `Retry-After` seconds; nothing was
reserved.

RenderFailed.description:
The page did not render: the host did not resolve, it never finished
loading, it timed out, or it was blocked. Try `delay_ms`, and check the
target loads in a normal browser.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page; empty on the final page.

total.description: How many templates the account has in total, independent of this page. Read it rather than counting pages.

code.description:
Stable, safe to branch on. New codes may be added: treat a
code you do not recognise as a failure of the class its HTTP
status indicates.

message.description: Human-readable. May change; do not match on it.

docs.description: Where the error codes are documented.

request_id.description: The X-Ironfang-Request-ID of the failed request. Quote it to support.

error.message: too many renders for that host, try again shortly

domain.description:
Required. Chromium silently drops a domainless cookie set before
navigation, so the render would quietly come back logged out.

Clip.description: A rectangle in CSS pixels from the top left of the page.

Margin.description:
Page margins in inches. Omitted sides keep Chromium's default rather
than becoming zero - a PDF printed hard to the paper edge is rarely
what leaving a field out was meant to mean.

PageAction.description:
One ordered pre-capture action. Selectors are CSS selectors in the main
page. click and hover wait until the first matching element is
interactable; wait_for_selector waits for its presence (not visibility).
All actions share the remaining timeout_ms render budget.

selector.description: Non-blank CSS selector; at most 1024 UTF-8 bytes.

duration_ms.description: Delay in milliseconds; all action delays together may total at most 10000 ms.

no_cache.description:
Force a fresh render instead of serving a cached one. Always
billable. Excluded from the cache key, so repeated fresh requests
do not collide.

block_ads.description:
Drop requests to known ad and tracker networks before they load.
Stopped as network requests rather than hidden afterwards, so the
page never spends time fetching them.

block_cookie_banners.description:
Hide common consent banners, and undo the scroll lock they set -
without which a full-page capture is one viewport tall.

Hidden, not accepted. Clicking "accept" would be a decision made
on the site owner's behalf and recorded as theirs.

hide_selectors.description:
CSS selectors to hide before capturing. Applied after load, so
elements injected by script are covered.

css.description:
Custom stylesheet, at most 65536 UTF-8 bytes. Applied after normal
load/wait conditions and built-in hiding, before script, actions,
settling and capture. Supports screenshots and PDFs, including
@media print rules. Malformed stylesheet syntax is a 400
bad_request; Chromium determines supported properties and values.

script.description:
JavaScript statements executed inside the target page's main-frame
context after load/wait conditions and css, before actions and
capture. Runs as an async function body: use await or return a
promise for asynchronous work. Completion is awaited; return values
are discarded. At most 16384 UTF-8 bytes and 5000 ms execution,
further bounded by the remaining timeout_ms budget. Syntax errors,
execution failures and timeouts return 422 render_failed with a
sanitized message. Supports screenshots and PDFs; no browser-session
or Playwright/Puppeteer APIs are exposed.

actions.description:
Up to 20 actions, executed in order after css and script, before
settling and capture. Supports screenshots and PDFs. Missing or
unready selectors and action timeouts fail with 422 render_failed,
identifying the zero-based action index and type. Invalid action
shapes are 400 bad_request. An action failure stops the list and is
not retried in queued jobs. All options, including action order,
are part of the screenshot cache key; use no_cache for a fresh run.

headers.description: Extra HTTP headers sent with every request for the page.

cookies.description:
Cookies to set before navigating. Set beforehand because a session
cookie that arrives after load has missed the request it was meant
to authenticate.

authorization.description:
Sets the `Authorization` header - the common case, spelled once.
An explicit `Authorization` in `headers` wins over this.

user_agent.description: Overrides the user agent, including any set by `device`.

wait_until.description:
When the page counts as ready. `networkidle` waits for traffic to
stop and is bounded by the render timeout, because a page with
polling never truly idles.

wait_for_selector.description:
Wait for this element before capturing. Fails the render if it
never appears, rather than returning a half-drawn page.

timeout_ms.description:
Per-render timeout. Clamped to the service maximum - it can lower
the ceiling but not raise it.

device_scale_factor.description: Pixel density. 2 is retina: the same CSS size at twice the pixels.

data.description: The payload - a URL, WiFi string, or any text up to 1KB.

size.description: Output side in pixels. Output is always square PNG.

ecc.description:
Error-correction level. Forced to `H` when a logo is present -
the logo destroys the modules it covers, and that budget has to
come from somewhere.

dark.description: Module color, `#rgb` or `#rrggbb`. Must actually be darker than `light`.

light.description:
Background color, or `transparent`. Transparent codes are
verified against a white ground - place them on light surfaces.

dots.description:
Module style. `circle` draws separated dots. Finder patterns
always render solid - styled finders are how QR generators
produce codes that do not scan.

invert.description:
Light modules on a dark ground. Explicit because it narrows the
audience: modern phone cameras read inverted codes, many
embedded and in-app scanners do not - use it for screens, not
print or payments. With the flag set, `dark` (the module color)
must be lighter than `light` (the ground). Verified against the
negative, so the structural guarantee holds.

logo.description:
Center mark as a base64 `data:` URI, png or jpeg, up to 1MB
decoded. Mutually exclusive with `logo_url`.

logo_url.description: Center mark by URL. SSRF-guarded and rate-capped like a render target.

logo_size.description: Logo tile as a fraction of the symbol width.

logo_pad.description: Knockout tile behind the logo so it sits on clean ground.

payload.description: Last posted body; omitted from lists and after purging.

JobDelivery.description:
Where this job goes when it finishes, by destination id. Register the
destination first; credentials are never sent here.

A webhook fires on success, failure and cancellation. Storage only
carries a result, so it fires on success alone - and a storage
delivery that gives up raises `render.delivery.failed` on the webhook
destination, which is how you find out that a bucket stopped
accepting uploads.

storage_key.description:
The object key, relative to the destination's prefix. Fixed text
plus `{job_id}`, `{external_id}` and `{date}` (`YYYY/MM/DD`) -
no other field, and nothing evaluated. Segments may hold letters,
digits, dot, dash and underscore; anything that would climb out
of the prefix is refused when the job is submitted, not quietly
rewritten. Defaults to `render/{date}/{job_id}`.

url.description: Page to capture. Mutually exclusive with `html`.

html.description: Markup to render. Mutually exclusive with `url`.

height.description: Viewport height. Ignored when `full_page` is set.

selector.description:
CSS selector of a single element to capture instead of the
viewport.

omit_background.description:
Transparent background instead of the page's own. Ignored for
`jpeg`, which has no alpha channel.

full_page_max_height.description:
Cap a `full_page` capture at this many pixels. An
infinite-scroll page has no natural end, so 20000 applies when
none is given, and is also the most that can be asked for.

format.description:
PNG is lossless and the default. WebP is typically a fraction of
the size for the same picture, which is what matters when the
output is served to browsers or social crawlers.

quality.description: Quality for the lossy formats, `jpeg` and `webp`. Ignored for PNG.

device.description:
Capture as a phone or tablet rather than a desktop window that
happens to be narrow. Sets the viewport, the device pixel ratio,
touch, and a matching mobile user agent together - width alone
gets media queries right and everything else wrong.

An explicit `width` or `height` still wins, so a preset can be
used for the density and user agent while overriding the size.

delay_ms.description:
Extra settle time after load. Ironfang Render watches the page and
captures when it stops changing, so this is rarely needed - use
it for content that arrives on a timer, which quiescence cannot
anticipate. Capped at ten seconds.

url.description: Public HTTP or HTTPS page to record.

width.description: Output and browser viewport width in pixels.

height.description:
Output and browser viewport height in pixels. Width multiplied
by height cannot exceed 1,200,000 pixels.

motion.description:
`per_page` moves one viewport at a time with eased transitions
and a 750ms reading pause. `single_sweep` makes one
continuous eased pass from top to bottom.

device.description: Use a full device preset. Explicit width and height still win.

delay_ms.description: Extra settle time after page load and before lazy-content preloading. Capped at ten seconds.

no_cache.description: Force a fresh recording instead of using a cached result.

ClipRequest.description:
Everything is optional. With no background a solid `colour` is used,
which is what most captioned clips want.

colour.description: Background colour, used when no background asset is given.

background.description: An image or video to fill the canvas, cropped to fit.

watermark.description: A PNG placed in the bottom right corner.

audio.description: An audio track, trimmed to the clip's length.

font_size.description: Caption size in pixels; defaults to a fifteenth of the width.

url.description: Page to print. Mutually exclusive with `html`.

html.description: Markup to print. Mutually exclusive with `url`.

paper_format.description:
Named page size. Omit for Chromium's default, which is Letter.
Sizes are portrait; `landscape` rotates them.

print_background.description:
Include background colours and images. Off by default, matching
a browser's print dialog.

kind.description:
`screenshot` signs a URL capture and requires `url`; `image` signs a
template render and requires `template`.

ttl_hours.description:
Hours until the URL expires. Leaving it out gives 720 (30 days);
`0` never expires.

path.description: Path only, for serving behind your own domain.

expires_at.description: When the URL stops rendering (UTC); null when it never expires.

Usage.description:
This UTC calendar month's usage of every Ironfang Render meter, from
the organisation's billing account. Amounts are pounds before tax, as
exact decimal strings.

period_end.description: The period as [period_start, period_end) in UTC dates.

catalogue_version.description: The billing catalogue version that prices this period.

mode.description: The billing account's mode; `enabled` means paid usage beyond the free allowances is on.

settled.description: What Ironfang Render's settled usage costs this period.

reserved.description: The most work in flight could add if it all succeeds; not charged on top of `settled`.

free_used.description: How much of `used` the free allowance covered.

reserved.description: Quantity held by work in flight.

remaining_free.description: Free allowance left once work in flight is counted.

free_utility.description: A meter that is never charged (QR codes).

exempt.description: The account is exempt from settling this product.

tags.name: Render
tags.description: Turn a URL or HTML into an image, PDF or video.

tags.name: Templates
tags.description: Stored HTML with `{{variable}}` placeholders, rendered on demand.

tags.name: Signed URLs
tags.description: Shareable render URLs that need no API key.

tags.name: Batches
tags.description: Up to 100 renders submitted, and refused, together.

tags.name: Destinations
tags.description: Where a finished job goes - a signed webhook, or your own S3 bucket.

tags.name: Account
tags.description: Usage this period, from the billing account.
